# Overview



**Turn any agent into a life science expert.** The NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit packages a decade of NVIDIA life sciences libraries, tools, and models as **31 ready-to-call agent skills** — each providing structured instructions, scripts, and references so a coding or scientific agent can select a tool, prepare inputs, run it, inspect outputs, and explain results. From protein folding and molecular docking to generative chemistry and de novo binder design, the toolkit bridges the gap between a general-purpose agent and domain-specific scientific computation.

![NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit](https://github.com/NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit/blob/main/assets/image.jpg?raw=true)

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L10), [docs/skill-card.md](/docs/skill-card.md#L1-L8)

## What Is a Skill?

A **skill** is a self-contained directory whose centerpiece is a `SKILL.md` file — a YAML frontmatter block (name, description, license, allowed tools) followed by Markdown instructions that teach an agent *how* to perform a specific scientific task. Skills may also ship `references/` directories with progressive-disclosure detail (API schemas, parameter tuning, validation checks, examples), `scripts/` with helper code, and `evals/` with deterministic test cases for quality assurance. When an agent loads a skill, it gains the domain knowledge to route a user's scientific intent to the correct API endpoint, construct a valid payload, execute the call, and interpret the response — without the user needing to know any API contract.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L162-L167), [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L21)

## Architecture at a Glance

The toolkit organizes skills into **three canonical types** by deployment model, plus **multi-step workflows** that compose individual skills into scientific pipelines. A nightly sync reconciles skills vendored from external source repositories, while a plugin build step aggregates all skills into distributable payloads for agent marketplaces.

```mermaid

    subgraph "Skill Sources"
        NIM["NIM Skills<br/>(10 single-NIM + 2 meta-skills)"]
        LIB["Library Skills<br/>(4 CUDA-X / GPU library skills)"]

        WF["Workflows<br/>(2 binder-design routes)"]
    end

    subgraph "Skill Internals"
        SM["SKILL.md<br/>YAML frontmatter + instructions"]
        REF["references/<br/>API · science · parameters · examples"]

        SCR["scripts/<br/>helper Python / shell"]
    end

    subgraph "Distribution"
```

## Skill Types

The three deployment models determine how a skill's underlying tool is accessed — hosted cloud API, local GPU library call, or self-hosted model container.

| Type | Deployment Model | Count | Authentication | GPU Required |
|------|-----------------|-------|----------------|--------------|
| **NIM Skills** | Hosted NVIDIA API (`health.api.nvidia.com`) or local Docker container | 10 single + 2 meta | `NGC_API_KEY` Bearer token (hosted); none after readiness (local) | Only for local Docker path |
| **Library Skills** | Direct Python/CUDA library call in user's environment | 4 | None | Yes — CUDA 12.6+ and NVIDIA GPU |
| **Open Model Skills** | User-cloned model repo + optional Docker container | 13 (8 KERMT + 5 Proteina-Complexa) | `NGC_API_KEY` for container pulls; `WANDB_API_KEY` optional for training | Yes — for training, inference, and evaluation |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L39-L61), [library-skills/nvmolkit-usage/SKILL.md](/library-skills/nvmolkit-usage/SKILL.md#L36-L46), [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L22-L36)

## The Skill Catalog

### NIM Skills — Cloud-Native BioNeMo Microservices

Each NIM skill wraps a single NVIDIA Inference Microservice with hosted and local Docker paths, full API reference, and validation guidance.

| Skill | Domain | What It Does |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| **boltz2-nim** | Structure prediction | Biomolecular complex structure + binding affinity (pIC50) |
| **diffdock-nim** | Molecular docking | Small-molecule binding-pose prediction |
| **evo2-nim** | Genomics | DNA sequence generation and variant effect scoring |
| **genmol-nim** | Generative chemistry | De novo molecule generation, scaffold decoration, lead optimization |
| **molmim-nim** | Generative chemistry | Latent-space molecule generation and interpolation |
| **msa-search-nim** | Sequence alignment | Multiple sequence alignments via ColabFold/MMseqs2 |
| **openfold2-nim** | Structure prediction | Monomer protein structure prediction |
| **openfold3-nim** | Structure prediction | Biomolecular complex structure prediction |
| **proteinmpnn-nim** | Protein design | Inverse folding / sequence design for a target backbone |
| **rfdiffusion-nim** | Protein design | De novo protein backbone and binder design |

### Meta-Skills — Multi-NIM Workflows

| Skill | Pipeline |
|-------|----------|
| **drug-discovery-pipeline** | GenMol → DiffDock → Boltz2 (generate → dock → score affinity) |
| **msa-structure-prediction-pipeline** | MSA-Search → OpenFold3 (align → predict structure) |

### Library Skills — GPU-Accelerated CUDA-X Libraries

| Skill | Library | What It Does |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| **nvmolkit-usage** | nvMolKit | GPU-batched Morgan fingerprints, Tanimoto similarity, ETKDG conformers, MMFF optimization, Butina clustering, substructure search |
| **parabricks** | Parabricks | Accelerated genomic secondary analysis (BWA-MEM2, GATK4, somatic workflows) |
| **genomics-workflow-acceleration** | Parabricks | Workflow-level genomic pipeline orchestration |
| **cuequivariance** | cuEquivariance | Build equivariant neural-network primitives (segmented tensor products, CG coefficients) |

### Open Model Skills — Self-Hosted Research Models

| Skill Group | Sub-Skills | What It Does |
|-------------|-----------|-------------|
| **KERMT** | setup, pretrain-scratch, continue-pretrain, add-cmim-pretrain, finetune, embed, infer, monitor | Graph neural network for molecular property prediction (ADMET); multi-task GROVER extension with cuik-molmaker data loading |
| **Proteina-Complexa** | setup, target, design, evaluate-pdbs, sweep | Flow-based generative protein binder design with inference-time optimization (beam, FK-steering, MCTS) |

### Workflows — End-to-End Scientific Pipelines

| Workflow | Routes | What It Does |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| **Generative Protein Binder Design** | `complexa-binder-design` (Proteina-Complexa) · `protein-binder-design` (RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + Boltz2/OpenFold3) | De novo binder design: resolve target + hotspots → generate binders → co-fold → rank by interface metrics |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L39-L61), [nim-skills/meta-skills/README.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/README.md#L1-L15), [workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/README.md](/workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/README.md#L1-L16), [open-models-skills/proteina-complexa/README.md](/open-models-skills/proteina-complexa/README.md#L1-L16)

## Project Structure

```
bionemo-agent-toolkit/
├── nim-skills/                  # NIM microservice skills (canonical / native)
│   ├── boltz2-nim/              #   SKILL.md + references/ + evals/ + config/
│   ├── diffdock-nim/
│   ├── ...
│   └── meta-skills/             # Multi-NIM pipeline compositions
│       ├── drug-discovery-pipeline/
│       └── msa-structure-prediction-pipeline/
├── library-skills/              # CUDA-X / GPU library skills
│   ├── nvmolkit-usage/
│   ├── parabricks/
│   ├── genomics-workflow-acceleration/
│   └── cuequivariance/
├── open-models-skills/          # Self-hosted open model skills (sourced)
│   ├── kermt/                   #   8 sub-skills (setup → pretrain → finetune → infer)
│   └── proteina-complexa/       #   5 sub-skills (setup → target → design → evaluate → sweep)
├── workflows/                   # End-to-end scientific workflows
│   └── generative-protein-binder-design/
├── components.d/                # Source repo declarations for nightly sync
├── compliance.d/                # Compliance artifacts (skill cards) for sourced skills
├── plugins.d/                   # Plugin build manifests (marketplace packaging)
├── skills/                      # Generated aggregate payload (skills.sh distribution)
├── docs/                        # Skill card, sync findings
├── scripts/                     # plugin_sync.py (aggregate freshness enforcer)
└── catalog-exceptions.yml       # Prune-safe exceptions for native skills
```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L162-L167), [components.d/kermt.yml](/components.d/kermt.yml#L1-L16), [catalog-exceptions.yml](/catalog-exceptions.yml#L1-L34)

## How Skills Get Into the Catalog

Skills arrive in the catalog through two channels, governed by the `components.d/` registry and the nightly sync workflow:

- **Native skills** (authored in-repo): NIM skills, workflows, and certain library skills live in this repository as the source of truth. They are never overwritten by sync.
- **Sourced skills** (vendored from external repos): Each entry in `components.d/*.yml` declares a source repository, branch ref, and path mapping. A nightly CI workflow rsyncs skills from those repos into their catalog directories (e.g., `open-models-skills/kermt/`). The `catalog-exceptions.yml` file protects native skills inside scanned roots from being pruned by the orphan detector.

After sync, `scripts/plugin_sync.py` enforces two invariants: **coverage** (every distributable source skill appears in `skills.sh.json`) and **freshness** (the aggregate payload under `skills/bionemo-agent-toolkit/` is an exact copy of each source skill). This runs as `--check` in CI and `--write` by contributors.

> [!TIP]
> The `--delete` flag on the nightly rsync means any file committed directly into a sourced catalog directory is wiped on the next sync. Compliance artifacts (`skill-card.md`) live in `compliance.d/` and are backfilled only when upstream doesn't yet ship its own card — upstream always wins.

Sources: [components.d/nvmolkit.yml](/components.d/nvmolkit.yml#L1-L10), [compliance.d/README.md](/compliance.d/README.md#L1-L28), [scripts/plugin_sync.py](/scripts/plugin_sync.py#L1-L27), [catalog-exceptions.yml](/catalog-exceptions.yml#L1-L34)

## Installation and Agent Compatibility

Skills install via the portable [`skills` CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), which copies a skill's `SKILL.md` and supporting files into the target agent's configuration directory:

```bash
# Interactive — pick a skill + install destination
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit

# One skill, no prompts
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill boltz2-nim --yes

# Target a specific agent (repeatable)
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill boltz2-nim --agent claude-code
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill boltz2-nim --agent codex

# Browse the catalog without installing
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --list
```

The repository also ships **native plugin marketplaces** for Claude Code (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) and Codex (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`), so the toolkit installs through each agent's native plugin flow as well. The `plugins.d/_defaults.yml` sets brand color (`#76b900`), capabilities (`Interactive`, `Write`), and the dual license across all plugins.

| Agent | Installation Path | Status |
|-------|-------------------|--------|
| **Claude Code** | Native plugin marketplace | Repo-verified |
| **Codex** | Native plugin marketplace | Repo-verified |
| **Any SKILL.md-compatible agent** | `npx skills add` CLI | Portable format |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L16-L37), [plugins.d/_defaults.yml](/plugins.d/_defaults.yml#L1-L25), [docs/skill-card.md](/docs/skill-card.md#L50-L53)

## License

The toolkit is **dual-licensed**: source code (scripts, tests, build tooling) under **Apache-2.0**; skills and documentation (SKILL.md files, workflows, READMEs) under **CC-BY-4.0**. The `pyproject.toml` declares this as `Apache-2.0 OR CC-BY-4.0` and pins the three runtime dependencies (`biotite`, `numpy`, `pyyaml`) used by the helper scripts shipped inside workflow skills. The repository is a catalog, not an installable Python package — the manifest exists so that NVIDIA nSpect / Black Duck can resolve the dependency tree from `uv.lock`.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L168-L177), [pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L1-L52)

# Quick Start



Get a life-science-capable agent running in under five minutes. The NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit packages **31 ready-to-call skills** — protein folding, molecular docking, generative chemistry, genomics, protein design, and more — into structured instructions any coding agent can follow. Each skill carries the domain knowledge a general-purpose agent lacks: endpoint contracts, input preparation, parameter selection, output interpretation, and validation checks. You express intent in scientific terms; the skill translates that into correct API calls.

![NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit](<NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit_github_url>/blob/main/assets/image.jpg?raw=true)

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L177), [docs/skill-card.md](/docs/skill-card.md#L1-L188)

## Prerequisites

Before installing skills, confirm your environment meets these baseline requirements:

| Requirement | Purpose | When Needed |
|---|---|---|
| **Agent harness** (Claude Code, Codex, or any `SKILL.md`-compatible agent) | Reads and executes skill instructions | Always |
| **`NGC_API_KEY`** (or `NVIDIA_API_KEY`) | Authenticates to hosted NVIDIA NIM endpoints on `health.api.nvidia.com` | Any hosted NIM skill call |
| **Docker + NVIDIA Container Toolkit** | Runs self-hosted NIM containers, Parabricks, or KERMT | Local NIM deployment, Parabricks, open-model skills |
| **NVIDIA GPU** | GPU-accelerated local inference | Parabricks, nvMolKit, cuEquivariance, KERMT, Proteina-Complexa; **not** needed for hosted-NIM paths |
| **Python ≥ 3.10** with `biotite`, `numpy`, `pyyaml` | Binder-design helper scripts | Protein binder design workflows |

> [!TIP]
> Hosted NIM paths require only an `NGC_API_KEY` and an HTTP client — no local GPU, no Docker. Start with hosted mode to validate your workflow before investing in local deployment.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L13-L32), [pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L1-L52), [docs/skill-card.md](/docs/skill-card.md#L33-L48)

## Install a Skill

Skills install through the [`skills` CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) — a lightweight `npx`-based tool that copies structured skill directories into your agent's configuration. The toolkit also ships native plugin marketplaces for **Claude Code** and **Codex**, so skills are discoverable through each agent's built-in plugin flow as well.

### Interactive Install (Recommended for First Use)

```bash
# Browse the catalog and pick a skill + install destination
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit
```

This opens an interactive picker showing all available skills. Select one and choose where to install it.

### One-Line Install (No Prompts)

```bash
# Install a specific skill without any prompts
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill boltz2-nim --yes
```

### Target a Specific Agent

```bash
# Install the same skill into multiple agents
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill diffdock-nim --agent claude-code
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill diffdock-nim --agent codex
```

### Browse Without Installing

```bash
# List all available skills — nothing is written to disk
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --list
```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L15-L31)

## Skill Types at a Glance

| Category | Count | Deployment | Example Skills |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NIM Skills** | 10 | Hosted API or local Docker | Boltz-2, DiffDock, Evo 2, GenMol, MolMIM, MSA-Search, OpenFold2, OpenFold3, ProteinMPNN, RFdiffusion |
| **Library Skills** | 4 | Local Python + GPU | nvMolKit, Parabricks, cuEquivariance, Genomics Workflow Acceleration |
| **Open Model Skills** | 2 | Local clone + GPU | KERMT (ADMET), Proteina-Complexa (binder design) |
| **Workflow Skills** | 3 | Multi-step NIM orchestration | Drug Discovery Pipeline, Protein Binder Design, MSA Structure Prediction |

## Your First Skill Call: Boltz-2 Structure Prediction

Here is a complete working example using the **Boltz-2 NIM** in hosted mode — the fastest path from install to result. This predicts the 3D structure of a protein sequence and returns an mmCIF file with confidence scores.

### Step 1: Install the Skill

```bash
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill boltz2-nim --yes
```

### Step 2: Set Your API Key

```bash
export NGC_API_KEY="nvapi-..."
```

### Step 3: Run the Prediction

Once the skill is installed in your agent, simply describe what you want in natural language:

> *"Predict the structure of insulin using Boltz2. The sequence is MALWMRLLPLLALLALWGPDPAAAFVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKTRREAEDLQVGQVELGGGPGAGSLQPLALEGSLQKRGIVEQCCTSICSLYQLENYCN. Use the hosted NVIDIA API."*

The agent reads the installed `SKILL.md`, constructs the correct endpoint URL, formats the payload, authenticates with your `NGC_API_KEY`, executes the request, and saves the resulting `.cif` structure file.

### What the Agent Executes Under the Hood

```python
import os
import requests

url = "https://health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/mit/boltz2/predict"
headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('NGC_API_KEY')}",
}

payload = {
    "polymers": [{
        "id": "A",
        "molecule_type": "protein",
        "sequence": "MALWMRLLPLLALLALWGPDPAAAFVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKTRREAEDLQVGQVELGGGPGAGSLQPLALEGSLQKRGIVEQCCTSICSLYQLENYCN",
    }],
    "recycling_steps": 3,
    "sampling_steps": 50,
    "diffusion_samples": 1,
    "step_scale": 1.638,
    "output_format": "mmcif",
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=300)
result = response.json()
# result contains: structures (mmCIF), confidence_scores
```

The skill's `SKILL.md` contains all of this — endpoint URLs, payload schemas, authentication patterns, output parsing, and validation steps — so the agent never has to guess.

Sources: [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L147), [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/evals/evals.json](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/evals/evals.json#L1-L166)

## Common Skill Patterns

Every skill follows the same structural contract. Understanding the pattern for one skill transfers to all others.

### Hosted vs. Local: The Universal Decision Point

Every NIM skill begins with a mode choice — **hosted API** or **local Docker** — and the pattern is consistent across all of them:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Mode Choice"] --> B["Hosted NVIDIA API"]
    A --> C["Local Docker"]
    B --> D["URL: health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/..."]
    B --> E["Auth: Bearer $NGC_API_KEY"]
    B --> F["No GPU required"]
    C --> G["URL: localhost:8000/..."]
    C --> H["Auth: None after readiness"]
    C --> I["GPU + Docker required"]
    C --> J["Health check: /v1/health/ready"]
```

| Aspect | Hosted | Local Docker |
|---|---|---|
| **URL prefix** | `https://health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/...` | `http://localhost:8000/...` (no `/v1/`) |
| **Authentication** | `Authorization: Bearer $NGC_API_KEY` on every request | No auth after container readiness |
| **GPU** | Not required | Required (varies by NIM) |
| **Startup** | Immediate | `docker login nvcr.io` → `docker run` → health check loop |
| **Data privacy** | Inputs sent to NVIDIA cloud | Inputs stay on your machine |
| **Cost** | API credits | Your GPU time |

### Skill Directory Anatomy

Every skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` (the primary instruction file with YAML frontmatter) plus optional reference and evaluation files:

```
nim-skills/boltz2-nim/
├── SKILL.md              ← Agent reads this (instructions + metadata)
├── references/
│   ├── api.md            ← Exact endpoints, schemas, Docker flags
│   ├── science.md        ← Purpose, strengths, limitations
│   ├── parameters.md     ← Tuning parameters
│   ├── validation.md     ← Output sanity checks
│   └── examples.md       ← Compact payload patterns
└── evals/
    ├── config.yml        ← Evaluation harness configuration
    └── evals.json        ← Functional + trigger evaluation cases
```

The `SKILL.md` is self-contained for first-pass usage. The agent loads `references/` files only when deeper detail is needed — this progressive-disclosure pattern keeps the agent's context window efficient.

Sources: [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L25), [nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L30), [nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L30)

## Skill Selection Guide

Use this decision table to identify the right skill for your scientific task:

| Your Goal | Skill to Install | Install Command |
|---|---|---|
| Predict protein/biomolecular structure | `boltz2-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill boltz2-nim --yes` |
| Predict monomer protein structure | `openfold2-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill openfold2-nim --yes` |
| Predict biomolecular complex structure | `openfold3-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill openfold3-nim --yes` |
| Dock a small molecule to a protein | `diffdock-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill diffdock-nim --yes` |
| Generate/analyze DNA sequences | `evo2-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill evo2-nim --yes` |
| Generate drug-like molecules | `genmol-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill genmol-nim --yes` |
| Optimize molecules in latent space | `molmim-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill molmim-nim --yes` |
| Build multiple sequence alignments | `msa-search-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill msa-search-nim --yes` |
| Design sequences for a target backbone | `proteinmpnn-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill proteinmpnn-nim --yes` |
| Design de novo protein backbones/binders | `rfdiffusion-nim` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill rfdiffusion-nim --yes` |
| Accelerated cheminformatics (GPU) | `nvmolkit-usage` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill nvmolkit-usage --yes` |
| Accelerated genomic analysis | `parabricks` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill parabricks --yes` |
| End-to-end virtual screening | `drug-discovery-pipeline` | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill drug-discovery-pipeline --yes` |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L34-L61), [plugins.d/bionemo-agent-toolkit.yml](/plugins.d/bionemo-agent-toolkit.yml#L20-L44)

## Running a Multi-Step Workflow

Workflows compose multiple NIM skills into end-to-end scientific pipelines. The **Drug Discovery Pipeline** is a canonical example — it chains GenMol → DiffDock → Boltz2 in a single orchestrated flow:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["GenMol"] -->|"SMILES candidates"| B["DiffDock"]
    B -->|"Ranked poses"| C["Boltz2"]
    C -->|"pIC50 + P(bind)"| D["Scored & Ranked Candidates"]
```

Install the workflow skill the same way:

```bash
npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill drug-discovery-pipeline --yes
```

Then describe your goal in natural language:

> *"Generate 30 drug-like molecules targeting this protein, dock them, and score binding affinity using the hosted API."*

The agent orchestrates all three NIMs sequentially — generating candidates with GenMol, docking each to the target protein with DiffDock, and predicting binding affinity with Boltz2 — producing a ranked table of candidates with QED scores, docking confidence, and pIC50 values.

Sources: [nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md#L1-L60), [workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/README.md](/workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/README.md#L1-L16)

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `401 Unauthorized` on hosted NIM call | Missing or invalid `NGC_API_KEY` | `export NGC_API_KEY="nvapi-..."` and verify at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com) |
| `422 Unprocessable Entity` | Invalid sequence, SMILES, or payload shape | Check the skill's `references/validation.md` for input requirements |
| Local NIM returns `404` | Used hosted URL path on local container (or vice versa) | Local paths omit `/v1/`; check the skill's `references/api.md` for the correct URL |
| Container health check loops forever | NIM still downloading model weights on first run | Wait — Boltz2 downloads ~30 GB on first start; monitor with `docker logs` |
| `NGC_API_KEY` not found in `.env` | Shell env not sourced | The skill's preflight loads `.env` only if it exists; prefer exporting directly |
| Agent picks wrong skill for "predict structure" | Overlapping descriptions (Boltz-2 vs OpenFold2 vs OpenFold3) | Specify the model name explicitly in your prompt |

> [!TIP]
> Every NIM skill's `SKILL.md` includes a **Limits And Troubleshooting** section with model-specific error codes, payload constraints, and common pitfalls. When an agent call fails, ask the agent to consult that section before retrying.

Sources: [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L130-L147), [nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md#L105-L119), [nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md#L148-L164)

# Skill Catalog



The **NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit** ships over **30 production-ready skills** that transform any coding or scientific agent into a life-science expert. Each skill is a self-contained directory containing a `SKILL.md` instruction file, optional `references/` for deeper context, optional `scripts/` for helper code, and `evals/` for validation. This catalog organizes every skill into four families — **NIM Skills**, **Library Skills**, **Open Model Skills**, and **Workflows** — so you can quickly find the right tool for your biological task.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L177), [skills.sh.json](/skills.sh.json#L1-L58)

## How the Catalog Is Organized

Skills live under four root directories in the repository, each representing a distinct provenance and deployment model. The [`skills.sh.json`](/skills.sh.json) grouping file defines how these skills appear in the `npx skills add` interactive picker and in plugin marketplace listings.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Catalog["bionemo-agent-toolkit"] --> NIM["nim-skills/<br/>NIM Microservices<br/>(10 atomic + 2 meta)"]
    Catalog --> LIB["library-skills/<br/>CUDA-X Libraries<br/>(4 skills)"]
    Catalog --> Open["open-models-skills/<br/>Open Models<br/>(8 KERMT + 5 Complexa)"]
    Catalog --> WF["workflows/<br/>Multi-Step Workflows<br/>(2 skills)"]

    NIM --> N1["boltz2-nim"]
    NIM --> N2["diffdock-nim"]
    NIM --> N3["evo2-nim"]
    NIM --> N4["genmol-nim"]
    NIM --> N5["molmim-nim"]
    NIM --> N6["msa-search-nim"]
    NIM --> N7["openfold2-nim"]
    NIM --> N8["openfold3-nim"]
    NIM --> N9["proteinmpnn-nim"]
    NIM --> N10["rfdiffusion-nim"]
    NIM --> META["meta-skills/"]
    META --> M1["drug-discovery-pipeline"]
    META --> M2["msa-structure-prediction-pipeline"]

    LIB --> L1["nvmolkit-usage"]
    LIB --> L2["parabricks"]
    LIB --> L3["cuequivariance"]
    LIB --> L4["genomics-workflow-acceleration"]

    OPEN --> O1["kermt/ (8 skills)"]
    OPEN --> O2["proteina-complexa/ (5 skills)"]

    WF --> W1["protein-binder-design"]
    WF --> W2["complexa-binder-design"]

    style NIM fill:#76b900,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style LIB fill:#4A90D9,stroke:#333,color:#fff
    style OPEN fill:#D4A017,stroke:#333,color:#000
    style WF fill:#C0392B,stroke:#333,color:#fff
```

| Family | Root Directory | Skill Count | Deployment Model |
|--------|---------------|-------------|-----------------|
| **NIM Skills** | `nim-skills/` | 12 (10 atomic + 2 meta) | Hosted NVIDIA API or local Docker NIM |
| **Library Skills** | `library-skills/` | 4 | Local Python library / CLI |
| **Open Model Skills** | `open-models-skills/` | 13 (8 KERMT + 5 Complexa) | Local Docker containers on your GPU |
| **Workflows** | `workflows/` | 2 | Multi-skill orchestration pipelines |

Sources: [skills.sh.json](/skills.sh.json#L1-L58), [README.md](/README.md#L47-L79)

## NIM Skills — Hosted API or Local Docker

NIM skills wrap **NVIDIA Inference Microservices (NIMs)** — containerized model endpoints that you can call via the hosted NVIDIA API (`health.api.nvidia.com`) or run locally with Docker. Every NIM skill follows a consistent pattern: choose mode → prepare inputs → call endpoint → save and validate output. Each ships `references/` files for API schemas, parameter tuning, validation checks, and science context.

| Skill | Directory | Scientific Domain | Key Capability |
|-------|-----------|-------------------|----------------|
| **Boltz-2** | `nim-skills/boltz2-nim/` | Structure & affinity | Biomolecular structure prediction + binding affinity (pIC50/IC50) |
| **DiffDock** | `nim-skills/diffdock-nim/` | Molecular docking | Small-molecule blind docking — ranked poses + confidence scores |
| **Evo 2** | `nim-skills/evo2-nim/` | Genomics | DNA sequence generation, variant scoring, and layer-output extraction |
| **GenMol** | `nim-skills/genmol-nim/` | Generative chemistry | De novo molecule generation, scaffold decoration, lead optimization (SAFE notation) |
| **MolMIM** | `nim-skills/molmim-nim/` | Generative chemistry | Latent-space molecule generation, CMA-ES guided optimization |
| **MSA-Search** | `nim-skills/msa-search-nim/` | Sequence alignment | GPU-accelerated MSA via ColabFold/MMSeqs2, paired MSA, PDB70 templates |
| **OpenFold2** | `nim-skills/openfold2-nim/` | Protein folding | Monomer protein structure prediction (AlphaFold2-like) |
| **OpenFold3** | `nim-skills/openfold3-nim/` | Protein folding | Biomolecular complex prediction (protein + DNA/RNA + ligands) |
| **ProteinMPNN** | `nim-skills/proteinmpnn-nim/` | Protein design | Inverse folding — sequence design for a target backbone |
| **RFdiffusion** | `nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/` | Protein design | De novo backbone and binder design, motif scaffolding |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L47-L79), [boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L10), [diffdock-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L10), [evo2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/evo2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L10), [genmol-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/genmol-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L10)

### NIM Meta-Skills — Composed Pipelines

Two **meta-skills** under `nim-skills/meta-skills/` orchestrate multiple NIM calls into common scientific workflows. They contain their own `SKILL.md` workflow instructions and `evals/` definitions, while delegating API-specific payloads to the individual NIM skills.

| Meta-Skill | Pipeline Sequence | Directory |
|-----------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Drug Discovery Pipeline** | GenMol → DiffDock → Boltz-2 (generate candidates, dock, score affinity) | `nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/` |
| **MSA Structure Prediction Pipeline** | MSA-Search → OpenFold3 (build alignment, predict structure) | `nim-skills/meta-skills/msa-structure-prediction-pipeline/` |

Sources: [nim-skills/meta-skills/README.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/README.md#L1-L15), [README.md](/README.md#L48-L53)

> [!TIP]
> All NIM skills share the same dual-mode pattern — hosted (`Authorization: Bearer $NGC_API_KEY`) or local Docker (no auth after readiness). When installing a NIM skill, set `NGC_API_KEY` in your environment for hosted access, or set `LOCAL_NIM_CACHE` for local deployment.

## Library Skills — GPU-Accelerated Libraries

Library skills provide agent-ready instructions for **CUDA-X accelerated Python libraries** — no NIM endpoints involved. The agent writes code that imports and calls these libraries directly. They are ideal when you need batch GPU throughput for cheminformatics or genomics operations on your own hardware.

| Skill | Directory | Library | Key Capability |
|-------|-----------|---------|----------------|
| **nvMolKit Usage** | `library-skills/nvmolkit-usage/` | `nvmolkit` | GPU-batched Morgan fingerprints, Tanimoto similarity, ETKDG conformers, MMFF optimization, Butina clustering |
| **Parabricks** | `library-skills/parabricks/` | `pbrun` CLI | Route individual Parabricks tools — FASTQ/BAM processing, RNA-seq, variant calling |
| **Genomics Workflow Acceleration** | `library-skills/genomics-workflow-acceleration/` | `pbrun` + workflow engines | Map CPU steps to GPU in existing Nextflow/Snakemake/WDL pipelines, with runtime toggles |
| **cuEquivariance** | `library-skills/cuequivariance/` | `cuequivariance` | Build equivariant neural-network primitives — segmented tensor products, CG coefficients, custom groups |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L72-L79), [nvmolkit-usage/SKILL.md](/library-skills/nvmolkit-usage/SKILL.md#L1-L10), [parabricks/SKILL.md](/library-skills/parabricks/SKILL.md#L1-L10), [cuequivariance/SKILL.md](/library-skills/cuequivariance/SKILL.md#L1-L10), [genomics-workflow-acceleration/SKILL.md](/library-skills/genomics-workflow-acceleration/SKILL.md#L1-L10)

## Open Model Skills — Local GPU Deployment

Open model skills wrap models that run **entirely on your local GPU infrastructure** via Docker containers. Unlike NIM skills, there is no hosted API option — you build the container image and run inference locally. These skill families are **multi-skill groups**: each model exposes a lifecycle of setup, training, and inference skills.

### KERMT — Molecular Property Prediction (8 Skills)

**KERMT** is a pretrained graph neural network for molecular ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) property prediction. It is a multi-task extension of GROVER with accelerated data loading. All eight skills share a common Docker image and depend on `kermt-setup` running first.

| Skill | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `kermt-setup` | Bootstrap environment — verify Docker + NVIDIA toolkit, build image, GPU smoke test |
| `kermt-pretrain-scratch` | Pretrain KERMT from scratch on your dataset |
| `kermt-continue-pretrain` | Continue pretraining from an existing checkpoint |
| `kermt-add-cmim-pretrain` | Add CMIM (conditional molecular information maximization) pretraining |
| `kermt-finetune` | Finetune a pretrained checkpoint for downstream ADMET tasks |
| `kermt-infer` | Run predictions with a finetuned checkpoint on a SMILES CSV |
| `kermt-embed` | Generate molecular embeddings from a checkpoint |
| `kermt-monitor` | Monitor training progress and resource usage |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L74-L75), [kermt-setup/SKILL.md](/open-models-skills/kermt/kermt-setup/SKILL.md#L1-L15), [kermt-infer/SKILL.md](/open-models-skills/kermt/kermt-infer/SKILL.md#L1-L15)

### Proteina-Complexa — Protein Binder Design (5 Skills)

**Proteina-Complexa** combines a pretrained flow-based generative model (built on La-Proteina) with inference-time optimization for high-quality binder generation. It supports three design pipelines: **protein binder** (default), **ligand binder** (small-molecule pocket), and **AME motif scaffolding** (enzyme design).

| Skill | Primary Tool | Purpose |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| `complexa-setup` | File-edit + CLI | Bootstrap environment, download model weights |
| `complexa-target` | File-edit | Register design targets in YAML configs |
| `complexa-design` | CLI (`complexa design`) | Run full design pipeline (generate → filter → evaluate → analyze) |
| `complexa-evaluate-pdbs` | CLI (`complexa analysis`) | Re-fold and score existing PDBs |
| `complexa-sweep` | Python script | Hyperparameter sweep over beam_width, nsteps, reward weights |

Sources: [proteina-complexa/README.md](/open-models-skills/proteina-complexa/README.md#L1-L52), [README.md](/README.md#L73-L74)

## Workflows — End-to-End Scientific Pipelines

Workflows are the highest-level skills in the catalog. They orchestrate multiple skill families (NIM skills, open model skills, custom scripts) into **complete scientific narratives** with validation, manifest generation, and branching logic. Workflows live under `workflows/` and are **native** to this repository — they are not synced from external sources.

| Workflow | Directory | Route | Pipeline Composition |
|----------|-----------|-------|---------------------|
| **Protein Binder Design** | `workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/protein-binder-design/` | NIM route | RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Boltz-2 (backbone → sequence → structure validation) |
| **Complexa Binder Design** | `workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/complexa-binder-design/` | Complexa route | Complexa design pipeline + Boltz-2 refolding + IPSAE interface analysis |

Both workflows share a `workflow-rules.mdc` rule file and a `references/route-selection.mdc` that helps the agent choose between the NIM route and the Complexa route based on available infrastructure and user intent.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L48-L50), [generative-protein-binder-design/README.md](/workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/README.md#L1-L52)

## Browsing and Installing Skills

The toolkit integrates with the [`skills` CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) for interactive discovery and installation. Use `--list` to browse without installing, or target a specific skill directly.

| Command | What It Does |
|---------|-------------|
| `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit` | Interactive picker — browse catalog and choose install destination |
| `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --list` | List all available skills without installing |
| `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit --skill boltz2-nim --yes` | Install one skill with no prompts |
| `npx skills add ... --agent claude-code` | Target a specific agent's skill directory (repeatable for multiple agents) |

The catalog grouping displayed by the picker is defined in [`skills.sh.json`](/skills.sh.json), which sorts skills into **BioNeMo NIMs**, **CUDA-X Libraries**, **Open Models**, and **Workflows** sections.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L17-L30), [skills.sh.json](/skills.sh.json#L1-L58)

# Architecture Overview



The NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit is a **skill-based architecture** that transforms life-science capabilities — protein folding, molecular docking, generative chemistry, genomics, and protein design — into self-contained, agent-consumable units. Each skill is an isolated directory anchored by a `SKILL.md` file (YAML frontmatter + structured instructions), optionally accompanied by `references/`, `evals/`, `config/`, and `scripts/`. The toolkit does not host infrastructure; it ships domain knowledge that lets any coding agent select, configure, invoke, and interpret BioNeMo tools correctly.

![NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit](<NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit_github_url>/blob/main/assets/image.jpg?raw=true)

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L177), [docs/skill-card.md](/docs/skill-card.md#L1-L188)

## Architectural Principles

The toolkit is governed by three first-principles design decisions that shape every layer of the system:

1. **Skill as atomic unit of capability.** A skill is the smallest distributable, evaluable, and composable unit. It carries everything an agent needs — trigger conditions, parameter contracts, request patterns, output interpretation, and troubleshooting — without requiring runtime infrastructure from the toolkit itself.

2. **Dual-origin catalog.** Skills originate from two sources: **native** skills authored directly in this repository (NIM skills, workflows), and **sourced** skills vendored from external NVIDIA repositories (KERMT, Proteina-Complexa, nvMolKit) via a nightly sync pipeline. This distinction determines how skills are maintained, validated, and governed.

3. **Aggregate payload for distribution.** The canonical installable payload lives under `skills/bionemo-agent-toolkit/skills/` — a generated mirror of the source skills. Distribution channels (skills.sh CLI, Codex marketplace, Claude Code plugin) all consume this aggregate, not the source directories directly.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L162-L167), [scripts/plugin_sync.py](/scripts/plugin_sync.py#L1-L27)

## System Architecture Diagram

The following diagram shows the end-to-end flow from skill authoring through distribution to agent consumption:


## Skill Taxonomy

The repository organizes skills into four distinct categories, each with a different origin pattern, deployment model, and maintenance contract:

| Category | Directory | Origin | Deployment Model | Count | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NIM Skills** | `nim-skills/` | Native (authored in-repo) | Hosted NVIDIA API or local Docker container | 12 | boltz2-nim, diffdock-nim, genmol-nim, rfdiffusion-nim |
| **Library Skills** | `library-skills/` | Native or sourced | Python library on GPU hardware | 4 | nvmolkit-usage, parabricks, cuequivariance |
| **Open Model Skills** | `open-models-skills/` | Sourced (vendored from external repos) | Local model training/inference with GPU | 13 | kermt-setup, complexa-design |
| **Workflows** | `workflows/` | Native (authored in-repo) | Multi-skill orchestration | 2 | protein-binder-design, complexa-binder-design |

**Meta-skills** (under `nim-skills/meta-skills/`) are a special sub-category of NIM skills that compose multiple single-NIM skills into pipeline workflows (e.g., GenMol → DiffDock → Boltz2 for drug discovery). They carry their own `SKILL.md` and `evals/` but delegate API specifics to the constituent skills.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L39-L61), [nim-skills/meta-skills/README.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/README.md#L1-L15), [skills.sh.json](/skills.sh.json#L1-L57)

## Skill Internal Structure

Every skill follows a uniform directory contract. The `SKILL.md` file is the only required artifact; all other directories are optional and loaded on demand:

```
<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md              # Required: YAML frontmatter + agent instructions
├── references/           # Optional: detailed API, science, parameter docs
│   ├── api.md            #   endpoint schemas, Docker flags
│   ├── science.md        #   purpose, strengths, limitations
│   ├── parameters.md     #   tuning guide
│   ├── validation.md     #   output sanity checks
│   └── examples.md       #   compact payload patterns
├── evals/                # Optional: evaluation definitions
│   ├── config.yml        #   Harbor/ACES configuration
│   ├── evals.json        #   functional eval cases + assertions
│   ├── trigger_evals.json#   trigger precision/recall labels
│   └── files/            #   eval fixture files (PDB, etc.)
├── config/               # Optional: tool config (e.g., skillspector baseline)
└── scripts/              # Optional: helper scripts for the skill
```

The `SKILL.md` frontmatter defines the skill's identity and activation contract:

| Frontmatter Field | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Unique skill identifier | `boltz2-nim` |
| `description` | Trigger description — agent matches this to decide activation | `Use Boltz2 NIM for biomolecular structure prediction...` |
| `license` | Dual-license declaration | `Apache-2.0 AND CC-BY-4.0` |
| `compatibility` | Runtime dependency constraints | `requests>=2.28` |
| `allowed-tools` | Agent tool permissions | `Bash, Read, Write, AskUserQuestion` |
| `metadata` | Extended metadata (owner, risk_tier) | `owner: ..., risk_tier: skill` |

Sources: [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [README.md](/README.md#L162-L167), [nim-skills/boltz2-nim](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim)

## Component Registry and Sourcing Pipeline

Skills vendored from external repositories are declared in `components.d/*.yml`. Each declaration specifies the source repository, branch ref, path to skills within that repo, and the target catalog directory:

| Component | Source Repo | Ref | Source Path | Catalog Directory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **KERMT** | `NVIDIA-BioNeMo/KERMT` | `main` | `agent/skills` | `open-models-skills/kermt` |
| **nvMolKit** | `NVIDIA-BioNeMo/nvMolKit` | `main` | `skills/nvmolkit-usage` | `library-skills/nvmolkit-usage` |
| **Proteina-Complexa** | `NVIDIA-BioNeMo/Proteina-Complexa` | `aggregator-compat` | `.claude/skills` | `open-models-skills/proteina-complexa` |

The nightly sync uses `rsync --delete` to mirror source skills into the catalog. Because `--delete` removes any file not present in the source, directly-authored files in sourced directories would be wiped — this is why compliance artifacts (`skill-card.md`) live in `compliance.d/` and are **backfilled** only when the rsync leaves no card in the catalog. As soon as upstream ships its own `skill-card.md`, the backfill becomes a no-op.

The `catalog-exceptions.yml` declares directories that are exempt from the orphan-pruning step. This includes the **native roots** (`nim-skills/`, `workflows/`) which are not scanned at all, and **native skills inside scanned roots** (e.g., `library-skills/parabricks`) that lack a public source repo and would otherwise be deleted by the pruner.

Sources: [components.d/kermt.yml](/components.d/kermt.yml#L1-L16), [components.d/nvmolkit.yml](/components.d/nvmolkit.yml#L1-L10), [components.d/proteina-complexa.yml](/components.d/proteina-complexa.yml#L1-L13), [catalog-exceptions.yml](/catalog-exceptions.yml#L1-L34), [compliance.d/README.md](/compliance.d/README.md#L1-L53)

## Aggregate Sync and Distribution

The `skills.sh.json` manifest is the central distribution config. It declares every distributable skill grouped into four categories — **BioNeMo NIMs**, **CUDA-X Libraries**, **Open Models**, and **Workflows** — with `notGrouped: "bottom"` controlling display order for ungrouped entries.

The sync script `plugin_sync.py` enforces two critical invariants:

1. **Coverage** — every distributable source skill (discovered by scanning `SOURCE_ROOTS` for `SKILL.md` files) must be listed in `skills.sh.json`. Unlisted skills are reported as coverage gaps.
2. **Freshness** — for every listed skill, the aggregate copy under `skills/bionemo-agent-toolkit/skills/<name>/` must be an exact byte-for-byte match of the source directory (excluding generated-only artifacts like `skill.oms.sig` and `BENCHMARK.md`).

The script operates in two modes: `--check` (CI gate, reports drift) and `--write` (contributor tool, rebuilds the aggregate). Aggregate-only artifacts (signatures, benchmark reports) survive a `--write` rebuild rather than being wiped, because they are generated by external signing/eval pipelines and not part of the source→aggregate sync contract.

Sources: [scripts/plugin_sync.py](/scripts/plugin_sync.py#L1-L55), [scripts/plugin_sync.py](/scripts/plugin_sync.py#L150-L198), [skills.sh.json](/skills.sh.json#L1-L57)

## Plugin Marketplace Integration

The toolkit ships self-hosted plugin marketplaces for agent-native installation:

| Channel | Mechanism | Config File |
|---|---|---|
| **skills.sh CLI** | `npx skills add NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit` | `skills.sh.json` |
| **Codex** | Native plugin marketplace | `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` |
| **Claude Code** | Native plugin marketplace | `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |

The `plugins.d/bionemo-agent-toolkit.yml` declares the plugin metadata (name, version, description, category, keywords) and curates which skills are included via `include_skills` — listing grouped paths (not flat `skills/<name>/`). Default fields (author, license, brand color, capabilities) are inherited from `plugins.d/_defaults.yml`, keeping per-plugin declarations minimal. The `skill_files: copy` strategy ensures real files are placed into the plugin tree (required for Codex local install), as opposed to symlinks back to canonical directories.

Sources: [plugins.d/bionemo-agent-toolkit.yml](/plugins.d/bionemo-agent-toolkit.yml#L1-L45), [plugins.d/_defaults.yml](/plugins.d/_defaults.yml#L1-L25), [README.md](/README.md#L33-L37)

## Evaluation Architecture

Each skill that ships evals follows a co-located pattern: `evals/` sits directly inside the skill directory. The evaluation system operates at two levels:

**Hosted Skill Lift (ACES/SkillEvaluator):** Each NIM skill provides a single, bounded `evals/evals.json` case plus `evals/config.yml`. The `astra-skill-eval` CLI converts the case into Harbor tasks and runs the same prompt both with and without the skill. The task requires a call to the real hosted NVIDIA NIM endpoint — whether the agent successfully discovers and executes that call is part of the measurement. The ACES default grader combines deterministic trajectory checks with LLM judgments.

**Eval case structure:** Each case in `evals.json` contains a natural-language `prompt`, an `expected_output` description, fixture `files`, and machine-checkable `assertions` that verify endpoint correctness, authentication, payload construction, and inter-skill data handoffs. Pipeline skills (e.g., drug-discovery-pipeline) include assertions validating that outputs from one NIM correctly feed into the next (e.g., GenMol SMILES → DiffDock ligand field).

The `evals/config.yml` declares the Harbor task source (`evals_json`) and required runtime environment variables (e.g., `NGC_API_KEY`), plus the grading mode (`aces_default`).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L62-L78), [nim-skills/boltz2-nim/evals/config.yml](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/evals/config.yml#L1-L10), [nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/evals/evals.json](/nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/evals/evals.json#L1-L167)

## Workflow Composition Pattern

Workflows compose multiple skills into multi-step scientific pipelines. Two composition mechanisms exist:

**Meta-skills** (under `nim-skills/meta-skills/`) are NIM-pipeline compositions that live in the NIM skill tree. Each meta-skill's `SKILL.md` contains the full orchestration instructions — step-by-step code for each NIM call, data handoff patterns between steps, and ranking/filtering logic. The Drug Discovery Pipeline, for example, sequences GenMol → DiffDock → Boltz2 with explicit SMILES handoffs, SAFE-notation encoding, and multi-stage ranking.

**Workflow rules** (`.mdc` files) provide route-selection logic. The `workflow-rules.mdc` in `workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/` acts as a dispatcher that helps the agent choose between two independent binder-design routes — Proteina-Complexa (reward-guided co-design) or RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + Boltz2 (classic diffusion + inverse-folding pipeline) — based on user intent.

```
Workflow Composition Hierarchy
├── Meta-Skills (sequential NIM pipelines)
│   ├── drug-discovery-pipeline: GenMol → DiffDock → Boltz2
│   └── msa-structure-prediction-pipeline: MSA-Search → OpenFold3
└── Workflows (route selection + multi-skill orchestration)
    ├── protein-binder-design: RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Boltz2/OpenFold3
    └── complexa-binder-design: Proteina-Complexa reward-guided co-design
```

Sources: [nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md#L1-L30), [workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/workflow-rules.mdc](/workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/workflow-rules.mdc#L1-L36), [workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/README.md](/workflows/generative-protein-binder-design/README.md#L1-L16)

## Visual Project Structure

The complete repository layout reveals the architectural layering — from source skills through build tooling to distribution artifacts:

```
bionemo-agent-toolkit/

```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L177), [scripts/plugin_sync.py](/scripts/plugin_sync.py#L37-L55)

## Key Architectural Invariants

Understanding these invariants is essential for contributing to or extending the toolkit:

| Invariant | Enforcement | Failure Mode |
|---|---|---|
| Every distributable skill has a `SKILL.md` | `plugin_sync.py --check` (coverage) | CI gate fails; skill invisible to distribution |
| Aggregate payload matches source exactly | `plugin_sync.py --check` (freshness) | CI gate fails; stale payload ships wrong instructions |
| Sourced skills are not directly edited in catalog | Nightly rsync with `--delete` | Local edits wiped on next sync |
| Compliance artifacts for sourced skills live in `compliance.d/` | Sync workflow backfill step | Cards deleted by rsync; backfill restores |
| Native skills in scanned roots are listed in `catalog-exceptions.yml` | `prune-orphans.sh` | Pruner deletes unlisted native skills |
| `plugins` symlink points to `skills/` | `plugin_sync.py` compatibility check | Migration compatibility breaks |

> [!TIP]
> When adding a new skill, you must: (1) create the skill directory with `SKILL.md` in the appropriate source root, (2) add the skill name to the correct grouping in `skills.sh.json`, and (3) run `python scripts/plugin_sync.py --write` to rebuild the aggregate. If the skill is sourced from an external repo, declare it in `components.d/` instead of authoring in-repo.

> [!TIP]
> The `evals/` directory is intentionally kept in the aggregate payload (not stripped) because NVCARPS Tier 3 live-agent eval validates the aggregate and requires the eval dataset to be present. Stripping it would cause Tier 3 to skip, invalidating coverage gates.

Sources: [scripts/plugin_sync.py](/scripts/plugin_sync.py#L44-L55), [scripts/plugin_sync.py](/scripts/plugin_sync.py#L150-L198), [compliance.d/README.md](/compliance.d/README.md#L1-L53), [catalog-exceptions.yml](/catalog-exceptions.yml#L1-L34)

# NIM Skills



NIM Skills are **portable runtime skill bundles** that wrap individual BioNeMo NIM (NVIDIA Inference Microservice) endpoints into agent-consumable workflows. Each skill encapsulates a single model's hosted API and local Docker deployment surface, providing structured instructions, reference schemas, validation criteria, and evaluation definitions — everything an AI agent needs to discover, invoke, and verify a BioNeMo model without human hand-holding. They are the atomic building blocks that [Meta-Skills](5-nim-skills) compose into multi-step scientific pipelines like [Drug Discovery Pipeline](8-drug-discovery-pipeline) and [MSA Structure Prediction Pipeline](10-msa-structure-prediction-pipeline).

Sources: [README.md](/nim-skills/README.md#L1-L15)

## NIM Skill Catalog

The toolkit ships **10 individual NIM skills** spanning four biomedical domains and **2 meta-skills** that orchestrate them into pipelines:

| Skill | Domain | Capability | Hosted Endpoint Base | Local Endpoint Base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `boltz2-nim` | Structure & Affinity | Biomolecular structure prediction + binding affinity (protein, DNA, RNA, ligand) | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/mit/boltz2/...` | `localhost:8000/biology/mit/boltz2/...` |
| `diffdock-nim` | Docking | Blind protein-ligand docking with ranked poses + confidence | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/mit/diffdock` | `localhost:8000/molecular-docking/diffdock/generate` |
| `evo2-nim` | Genomics | DNA sequence generation + local forward/layer-output extraction | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/arc/evo2-40b/...` | `$EVO2_NIM_URL/biology/arc/evo2/...` |
| `genmol-nim` | Molecule Design | De novo molecule generation, scaffold decoration, motif extension via SAFE notation | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/nvidia/genmol/...` | `localhost:8000/generate` |
| `molmim-nim` | Molecule Design | Latent-space molecule embedding, sampling, CMA-ES guided optimization | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/nvidia/molmim/...` | `localhost:8000/...` (multiple endpoints) |
| `msa-search-nim` | Structure & Affinity | GPU-accelerated MSA generation (UniRef30, ColabFold envdb, PDB70 templates) | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/colabfold/msa-search/...` | `localhost:8000/biology/colabfold/msa-search/...` |
| `openfold2-nim` | Structure & Affinity | Monomer protein structure prediction (AlphaFold2-like) | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/openfold/openfold2/...` | `localhost:8000/biology/openfold/openfold2/...` |
| `openfold3-nim` | Structure & Affinity | Multi-entity complex prediction (protein, DNA, RNA, ligand) | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/openfold/openfold3/...` | `localhost:8000/biology/openfold/openfold3/...` |
| `proteinmpnn-nim` | Protein Design | Inverse folding — sequence design for a target backbone PDB | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/ipd/proteinmpnn/...` | `localhost:8000/biology/ipd/proteinmpnn/...` |
| `rfdiffusion-nim` | Protein Design | De novo backbone design, motif scaffolding, binder design | `health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/ipd/rfdiffusion/...` | `localhost:8000/biology/ipd/rfdiffusion/...` |

Sources: [boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [diffdock-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [evo2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/evo2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [genmol-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/genmol-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [molmim-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/molmim-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [msa-search-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/msa-search-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [openfold2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/openfold2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [openfold3-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/openfold3-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [proteinmpnn-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/proteinmpnn-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8)

## Skill Directory Anatomy

Every NIM skill follows an identical layout, making the structure predictable and enabling automated tooling to discover, validate, and publish each skill uniformly:

```
nim-skills/<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md                    # Agent-facing runtime instructions (frontmatter + body)
├── config/
│   └── skillspector-baseline.yml   # SkillSpector false-positive suppression rules
├── evals/
│   ├── config.yml              # Harbor task source, required env vars, grading mode
│   ├── evals.json              # Task eval definitions with prompt + assertions
│   └── trigger_evals.json      # Skill-trigger classification tests (should/shouldn't activate)
└── references/
    ├── api.md                  # Exact endpoints, schemas, Docker flags, response fields
    ├── examples.md             # Compact hosted/local payload patterns and save snippets
    ├── parameters.md           # Parameter descriptions, ranges, and tuning effects
    ├── science.md              # Model purpose, strengths, limitations, handoffs
    └── validation.md           # Artifact and scientific sanity checks
```

The **`SKILL.md`** file is the primary contract — an agent reads it first for immediate usage guidance, then loads reference files only when the task requires deeper detail. The **`evals/`** directory defines how the skill's agent behavior is tested and validated (see [Evals Configuration](15-evals-configuration)). The **`config/`** directory houses compliance suppression rules audited against the [SkillSpector](18-compliance-and-security-model) static analyzer.

Sources: [README.md](/nim-skills/README.md#L6-L14), [skillspector-baseline.yml](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/config/skillspector-baseline.yml#L1-L19)

## SKILL.md Frontmatter Schema

The YAML frontmatter at the top of every `SKILL.md` encodes machine-readable skill metadata consumed by the agent runtime and the publishing pipeline:

```yaml
---
name: <skill-name>                          # Unique skill identifier (matches directory name)
description: >                              # Natural-language trigger description for agent routing
  <What the skill does and when to invoke it>
license: Apache-2.0 AND CC-BY-4.0           # Dual license for code + documentation
compatibility: "requests>=2.28"             # Python package requirements for the skill's code
allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Write, AskUserQuestion  # Tool primitives the agent may use
---
```

The **`name`** field is the canonical skill identifier used in eval routing, component registry sync, and meta-skill composition. The **`description`** is a densely packed trigger surface — it lists model names, task types, input formats, and deployment modes so that an agent's skill-selection heuristic can match user intent without ambiguity. The **`allowed-tools`** list constrains the agent's execution surface to a safe, auditable set of primitives.

Sources: [boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8), [evo2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/evo2-nim/SKILL.md#L1-L8)

## Dual-Mode Architecture: Hosted vs Local

Every NIM skill supports **two deployment modes** that share the same prediction logic but differ in endpoint routing, authentication, and infrastructure requirements. This dual-mode design is the central architectural pattern of the NIM skill layer:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Agent["AI Agent"]
        SKILL["SKILL.md<br/>Choose Mode"]
    end

    subgraph Hosted["Hosted Mode"]
        H_EP["health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/..."]
        H_AUTH["Authorization: Bearer $NGC_API_KEY"]
        H_NGC["NGC API Platform"]
    end

    subgraph Local["Local Mode"]
        L_EP["localhost:8000/biology/...<br/>(no /v1/ prefix)"]
        L_NOAUTH["No auth header<br/>after readiness"]
        L_DOCKER["Docker Container<br/>nvcr.io/nim/..."]
        L_HEALTH["/v1/health/ready<br/>polling loop"]
    end

    SKILL -->|"Hosted"| H_EP
    SKILL -->|"Local"| L_DOCKER
    H_EP --> H_AUTH --> H_NGC
    L_DOCKER --> L_HEALTH --> L_EP --> L_NOAUTH
```

### Mode Selection Protocol

Each `SKILL.md` begins with a **"Choose Mode"** section that follows a consistent protocol:

1. **Honor explicit configuration** — if `NIM_API_MODE` is set to `hosted` or `local`, use it without asking
2. **Infer from environment** — if a skill-specific URL variable is set (e.g., `EVO2_NIM_URL`, `PROTEINMPNN_NIM_URL`), treat it as local mode
3. **Ask only when ambiguous** — prompt the user only when neither the environment nor the user's request makes the mode clear

### Endpoint Routing Differences

The hosted and local paths are **not identical** — a common source of errors:

- **Hosted** endpoints use the `/v1/` prefix: `https://health.api.nvidia.com/v1/biology/...`
- **Local** endpoints **omit** `/v1/`: `http://localhost:8000/biology/...`
- Some skills have **structurally different** local paths (e.g., DiffDock local uses `/molecular-docking/diffdock/generate` while hosted uses `/v1/biology/mit/diffdock`)
- Some skills expose **local-only endpoints** not available on the hosted API (e.g., MolMIM's `/embedding`, `/hidden`, `/decode`, `/sampling`; Evo2's `/forward`)

> [!TIP]
> When debugging a local `404`, the most common cause is accidentally including the `/v1/` prefix on a local endpoint. Every NIM skill's troubleshooting section calls this out explicitly.

### Authentication Contract

| Aspect | Hosted | Local |
|---|---|---|
| Auth header | `Authorization: Bearer $NGC_API_KEY` | None (after readiness) |
| Key variable | `NGC_API_KEY` | `NGC_API_KEY` or `NVIDIA_API_KEY` (fallback for Docker login) |
| Key purpose | API request authorization | Container registry login + first-run model download |
| Key visibility | Never print or echo — confirm existence via shell tests | Same — never print keys |
| After readiness | N/A | No auth header on inference requests |

Sources: [boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L22-L36), [diffdock-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md#L21-L36), [evo2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/evo2-nim/SKILL.md#L23-L46), [molmim-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/molmim-nim/SKILL.md#L22-L57)

## Local Docker Deployment Pattern

The local deployment follows a rigorous **env preflight → registry login → container launch → readiness poll → inference** sequence. Every SKILL.md encodes the same contract to prevent common mistakes:

```bash
# 1. Env preflight — source .env, resolve key fallback, validate required vars
set -a
[ -f .env ] && . ./.env
set +a
if [ -z "${NGC_API_KEY:-}" ] && [ -n "${NVIDIA_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  export NGC_API_KEY="$NVIDIA_API_KEY"
fi
: "${NGC_API_KEY:?Set NGC_API_KEY or NVIDIA_API_KEY}"
: "${LOCAL_NIM_CACHE:?Set LOCAL_NIM_CACHE}"

# 2. Registry login
echo "$NGC_API_KEY" | docker login nvcr.io --username '$oauthtoken' --password-stdin

# 3. Container launch (image, GPU, cache mount, port vary per skill)
mkdir -p "${LOCAL_NIM_CACHE}"
docker run --rm --name <skill> --gpus all \
  --shm-size=<size> \
  -e NGC_API_KEY \
  -v "${LOCAL_NIM_CACHE}:/opt/nim/.cache" \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  nvcr.io/nim/<org>/<image>:<tag>

# 4. Readiness check
until curl -sf http://localhost:8000/v1/health/ready; do sleep 5; done

# 5. Inference (no Authorization header)
```

Key constraints enforced across all skills:

- **Never invent a `LOCAL_NIM_CACHE` default** — the user must set it explicitly
- **Never drop the `NVIDIA_API_KEY` fallback** — some environments set this instead of `NGC_API_KEY`
- **Never assume warm-cache key-free startup** — first-run downloads model weights and the time varies by image/version
- **Cache mount path varies** — most skills use `/opt/nim/.cache`, but ProteinMPNN uses `/home/nvs/.cache/nim`

### GPU Requirements by Skill

| Skill | Min VRAM | GPU Notes | First-Run Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boltz2 | ~16 GB | `--gpus all`, `--shm-size=16G` | ~30 GB model weights |
| DiffDock | ~24 GB | Single GPU | Moderate |
| Evo2 40B | 2×H100 80GB or 1×H200 141GB | **FP8 required** (compute capability ≥8.9); A100 incompatible | ~110 GB |
| Evo2 7B | H100/H200/RTX6000Ada/L40S | Set `NIM_VARIANT=7b` | ~50 GB |
| GenMol | Single GPU | `NIM_TEST_GPU=0` | ~20 GB |
| MolMIM | Single GPU | `NGC_CLI_API_KEY` mapping | Moderate |
| MSA-Search | GPU required | DB: 490 GB (UniRef30) to 1.4 TB (full) | 14 min (parallel) vs 80+ min (built-in) |
| OpenFold2 | Single GPU | ~80 GB disk, 64 GB RAM recommended | ~10 GB parameters |
| OpenFold3 | Single GPU | `--shm-size=16g` | ~10-15 GB model weights |
| ProteinMPNN | ~3 GB | Cache at `/home/nvs/.cache/nim` | Moderate |
| RFDiffusion | ~12 GB | Single GPU, `device=0` default | Moderate |

Sources: [boltz2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/SKILL.md#L38-L74), [evo2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/evo2-nim/SKILL.md#L48-L101), [msa-search-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/msa-search-nim/SKILL.md#L42-L106), [openfold3-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/openfold3-nim/SKILL.md#L46-L91), [proteinmpnn-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/proteinmpnn-nim/SKILL.md#L40-L57)

## Request Pattern Conventions

Every SKILL.md includes a **"Request Pattern"** section with a ready-to-execute Python snippet. These follow a consistent template:

```python
import os
import requests

HOSTED = True  # or os.getenv("NIM_API_MODE", "hosted").strip().lower() != "local"
url = (
    "<HOSTED_URL>"
    if HOSTED else "<LOCAL_URL>"
)
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
if HOSTED:
    headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {os.getenv('NGC_API_KEY')}"

payload = { ... }  # skill-specific fields
response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=300)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

Each skill documents its **payload gotchas** — non-obvious API quirks that trip up unfamiliar users:

| Skill | Key Gotcha |
|---|---|
| Boltz2 | MSA uses `alignment`/`format`/`rank`, not the stale `data` field; affinity requires `predict_affinity: True` on exactly one ligand |
| DiffDock | SMILES ligand uses `ligand_file_type: "txt"` (not `"smiles"`); strip PDB to ATOM records only |
| Evo2 | Field is `num_tokens` (not `max_tokens`); `/forward` is local-only, no hosted equivalent; A100 incompatible with FP8 |
| GenMol | `temperature` and `noise` are **strings** not floats; the `smiles` field takes SAFE notation, not raw SMILES |
| MolMIM | Field is `smi` (not `smiles`); `/embedding`, `/hidden`, `/decode`, `/sampling` are local-only |
| OpenFold2 | Monomer-only — hand off complexes to OpenFold3 or Boltz2; `selected_models` is 1-5 |
| OpenFold3 | Top level is `{"inputs": [...]}` with exactly one input; `molecules` supports 1-32 entities |
| ProteinMPNN | `sampling_temp` must be a list even for one value; cache mount is `/home/nvs/.cache/nim` |
| RFDiffusion | De novo requires a dummy PDB for hosted validation; `hotspot_res` uses `"A50"` strings, not tuples |

Sources: [genmol-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/genmol-nim/SKILL.md#L55-L109), [diffdock-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/diffdock-nim/SKILL.md#L54-L71), [molmim-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/molmim-nim/SKILL.md#L110-L127), [evo2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/evo2-nim/SKILL.md#L208-L221), [proteinmpnn-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/proteinmpnn-nim/SKILL.md#L91-L98), [rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md#L78-L99)

## Meta-Skills: Composing NIM Skills into Pipelines

The `nim-skills/meta-skills/` directory contains **composition skills** that chain multiple individual NIM skills into end-to-end scientific workflows. Unlike individual skills, meta-skills do not wrap a single API — they orchestrate a sequence of NIM calls, passing outputs from one step as inputs to the next.

### Drug Discovery Pipeline

**GenMol → DiffDock → Boltz2**: Generate drug-like molecules, dock them to a protein target, then predict binding affinity for the top docking hits. Supports de novo hit discovery, scaffold-based lead optimization, and virtual screening.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Step 1<br/>GenMol<br/>Generate molecules"] -->|"SMILES list<br/>ranked by QED/LogP"| B["Step 2<br/>DiffDock<br/>Dock to target"]
    B -->|"Top poses<br/>ranked by confidence"| C["Step 3<br/>Boltz2<br/>Predict affinity"]
    C -->|"pIC50 + P(binding)"| D["Final ranking<br/>by affinity"]
```

### MSA Structure Prediction Pipeline

**MSA-Search → OpenFold3**: Search for evolutionary homologs via GPU-accelerated MMSeqs2, then feed the A3M alignment into OpenFold3 for MSA-informed structure prediction — the full AlphaFold3-style pipeline.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Step 1<br/>MSA-Search<br/>Find homologs"] -->|"A3M alignment<br/>+ template hits"| B["Step 2<br/>OpenFold3<br/>Predict structure"]
    B -->|"PDB/CIF +<br/>confidence scores"| C["Validated<br/>structure"]
```

Meta-skills carry a distinct **privacy notice** in their frontmatter: molecule/sequence inputs and `NGC_API_KEY` are transmitted to external NVIDIA-hosted APIs on every call. The description explicitly advises using local NIM containers for confidential or proprietary data.

Sources: [meta-skills/README.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/README.md#L1-L15), [drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md#L1-L28), [msa-structure-prediction-pipeline/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/msa-structure-prediction-pipeline/SKILL.md#L1-L37)

## Evaluation and Trigger System

Each skill's `evals/` directory defines two evaluation layers:

**`evals.json`** contains **task evals** — structured test cases with a `prompt`, `expected_output`, and an `assertions` array. Each assertion has an `id`, `description`, and `check` (a natural-language predicate that the grading system evaluates against the agent's trajectory). Evals are split into immediate `evals` (run on every publish) and `deferred_evals` (awaiting infrastructure, like local Docker environments in Harbor). The config in `config.yml` specifies the Harbor task source, required environment variables (e.g., `NGC_API_KEY`), and grading mode.

**`trigger_evals.json`** contains **skill-routing classification tests** — pairs of `{query, should_trigger}` that verify the agent's skill-selection heuristic correctly activates the skill for relevant queries and **does not** activate it for unrelated ones. For example, Boltz2's trigger evals include protein structure queries as `should_trigger: true` and BLAST/molecular-weight queries as `should_trigger: false`.

Sources: [evals.json](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/evals/evals.json#L1-L166), [trigger_evals.json](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/evals/trigger_evals.json#L1-L23), [config.yml](/nim-skills/boltz2-nim/evals/config.yml#L1-L10)

## Skill Interconnections and Handoffs

NIM skills are not isolated — the SKILL.md bodies document explicit **handoff points** where one skill's output becomes another's input, forming a knowledge graph of biomedical workflows:

| From Skill | Handoff Trigger | To Skill | Data Passed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `msa-search-nim` | User needs MSA for structure prediction | `openfold2-nim` or `openfold3-nim` | A3M alignment → `alignments` or `msa` payload field |
| `rfdiffusion-nim` | Generated backbone PDB needs sequences | `proteinmpnn-nim` | `output_pdb` → `input_pdb` |
| `proteinEvo2-nim` | Designed sequences need structure validation | `boltz2-nim` or `openfold3-nim` | FASTA sequences → `sequence` or `polymers` field |
| `proteinmpnn-nim` | Designed sequences need structure validation | `boltz2-nim` or `openfold3-nim` | Multi-FASTA → prediction payload |
| `genmol-nim` | Generated molecules need docking | `diffdock-nim` | SMILES list → `ligand` field |
| `diffdock-nim` | Top docking poses need affinity scoring | `boltz2-nim` | Pose SDF + receptor → structure+affinity payload |

These handoffs are precisely what the meta-skills codify into executable pipelines, but they are also documented inline within each individual skill's `references/science.md` so that an agent can discover and chain them dynamically.

Sources: [openfold2-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/openfold2-nim/SKILL.md#L113-L115), [rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/rfdiffusion-nim/SKILL.md#L149-L154), [drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/drug-discovery-pipeline/SKILL.md#L22-L28), [msa-structure-prediction-pipeline/SKILL.md](/nim-skills/meta-skills/msa-structure-prediction-pipeline/SKILL.md#L33-L37)

## Next Steps

- **Understand the full SKILL.md format**: See [SKILL.md File Format](11-skill-md-file-format) for a deep dive into frontmatter fields and body structure
- **Choose your deployment**: See [Hosted vs Local NIM Deployment](12-hosted-vs-local-nim-deployment) for a detailed comparison of the two modes
- **Explore other skill types**: [Open Model Skills](6-open-model-skills) for training/fine-tuning workflows, [Library Skills](7-library-skills) for GPU-accelerated library integrations
- **Run a pipeline end-to-end**: [Drug Discovery Pipeline](8-drug-discovery-pipeline) or [MSA Structure Prediction Pipeline](10-msa-structure-prediction-pipeline)
- **Validate skill quality**: [Skill Lift Evaluation](14-skill-lift-evaluation) and [Evals Configuration](15-evals-configuration)

# Open Model Skills



Open Model Skills are the toolkit's **locally-deployed, container-native skill families** for NVIDIA's open-source BioNeMo models. Unlike [NIM Skills](5-nim-skills) that target cloud-hosted NIM endpoints, open model skills run the full model lifecycle — environment bootstrap, pretraining, finetuning, inference, embedding, and monitoring — inside Docker containers on your own GPU hardware. The toolkit currently ships two open model families: **KERMT** (molecular foundation model) and **Proteina-Complexa** (protein design pipeline), each organized as a directed acyclic graph of composable skills.

Sources: [kermt-setup/SKILL.md](open-models-skills/kermt/kermt-setup/SKILL.md#L1-L139), [complexa-setup/SKILL.md](open-models-skills/proteina-complexa/complexa-setup/SKILL.md#L1-L200), [proteina-complexa/README.md](open-models-skills/proteina-complexa/README.md#L1-L52)

## Architectural Overview

Open model skills share a common architectural DNA despite targeting fundamentally different scientific domains. Both families follow the same **setup → validate → prepare → launch → monitor** workflow pattern, both rely on Docker containers with GPU passthrough via `nvidia-container-toolkit`, and both emit replayable JSON manifests (`run.json` or `run_manifest.json`) that capture the exact invocation for reproducibility.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "KERMT Family (Molecular ML)"
        KS[kermt-setup] --> KCP[kermt-continue-pretrain]
        KS --> KPS[kermt-pretrain-scratch]
        KS --> KAC[kermt-add-cmim-pretrain]
        KS --> KFT[kermt-finetune]
        KS --> KI[kermt-infer]
        KS --> KE[kermt-embed]
        KCP --> KM[kermt-monitor]
        KPS --> KM
        KAC --> KM
        KFT --> KM
    end

    subgraph "Proteina-Complexa Family (Protein Design)"
        CS[complexa-setup] --> CT[complexa-target]
        CT --> CD[complexa-design]
        CS --> CD
        CD --> CE[complexa-evaluate-pdbs]
        CS --> CE
        CD --> CW[complexa-sweep]
    end
```

The diagram above captures the **invocation dependency graph**: setup skills are prerequisites for all downstream workflows, and monitor/evaluate skills are consumers of the artifacts those workflows produce.

Sources: [kermt-setup/SKILL.md](open-models-skills/kermt/kermt-setup/SKILL.md#L1-L139), [complexa-design/SKILL.md](open-models-skills/proteina-complexa/complexa-design/SKILL.md#L1-L200)

## Common Patterns Across Families

Despite their domain differences, both families share these architectural invariants:

| Pattern | KERMT | Proteina-Complexa |
|---|---|---|
| **Bootstrap skill** | `kermt-setup` — builds Docker image, GPU smoke test | `complexa-setup` — creates `.env`, downloads checkpoints, validates env |
| **Pre-flight gate** | `kermt_container.sh check_system` | `preflight.sh` → `preflight.json` |
| **Validation step** | `check_checkpoint.py` + `check_data.py` | `complexa validate env` / `complexa validate design` |
| **Data preparation** | `prepare_data.py` → `prepare_data.json` manifest | Hydra config resolution + `complexa download` |
| **Execution model** | Detached Docker containers (`run_detached`) | CLI-orchestrated subprocesses (`complexa design`) |
| **Replayability** | `run.json` with `cmd_replay` field | `run_manifest.json` via `write_manifest.py` |
| **Container base** | `nvidia/cuda:12.6.3-cudnn-devel-ubuntu22.04` | UV venv or Docker (user-selectable runtime) |
| **GPU requirement** | CUDA 12.6 capable, ≥1 GPU | ≥40 GB VRAM (A100/H100/L40S) |
| **License** | Apache-2.0 | Apache-2.0 |

> [!TIP]
> Every open model skill begins with a pre-flight check that validates GPU, disk, and dependencies *before* touching data. If the gate fails, the skill surfaces actionable errors and stops — it never silently proceeds on a misconfigured host.

Sources: [kermt-continue-pretrain/SKILL.md](open-models-skills/kermt/kermt-continue-pretrain/SKILL.md#L1-L200), [complexa-setup/SKILL.md](open-models-skills/proteina-complexa/complexa-setup/SKILL.md#L1-L200)

## KERMT Family — Molecular Foundation Model

**KERMT** (Knowledge-Enhanced Representation Model for Therapeutics) is an open molecular foundation model for SMILES-based molecular property prediction. The KERMT skill family provides **8 skills** covering the complete model lifecycle from environment setup through monitoring.

### Skill Inventory

| Skill | Classification | Purpose | Container Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kermt-setup` | atomic | Bootstrap Docker environment, build `kermt:latest` image, GPU smoke test | Blocking |
| `kermt-continue-pretrain` | workflow | Continue pretraining from an existing checkpoint (grover_base / cmim / hybrid) | Detached |
| `kermt-pretrain-scratch` | workflow | Pretrain a fresh model from scratch on a custom corpus | Detached |
| `kermt-add-cmim-pretrain` | workflow | Upgrade grover_base → hybrid by adding cMIM decoder, then continue pretraining | Detached |
| `kermt-finetune` | workflow | Finetune a pretrained encoder on a labeled CSV | Detached |
| `kermt-infer` | workflow | Run predictions with a finetuned checkpoint on SMILES-only CSV | Blocking |
